title: database-mcp database profiles
description: Named database connections ("profiles") served by one database-mcp process. Every MCP tool accepts an optional "profile" argument selecting one of these.

$schema.description: Path or URL to this schema. Ignored by the server; present so editors offer completion and hover docs.

_readme.description: Free-form notes. Any key starting with _ is ignored by the server.

defaultProfile.description: Name of the profile used when a tool call omits "profile". Optional when exactly one profile is defined; required once there are several.

profiles.description: One entry per database. The key is the profile name the AI passes as "profile".

propertyNames.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscore, starting with a letter, max 32 characters. Reserved: all, default, none, profiles, list.

engine.description: Database engine. Only "postgres" is implemented today; the others are reserved.

description.description: Human-readable note shown to the AI by list_databases, e.g. "Production SaaS". Helps it pick the right database.

comment.description: Free-form note. Any key starting with _ is ignored by the server.

ssl.description: Force SSL on or off. Omit to auto-detect: enabled for every host except localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1. In url style this overrides ?sslmode=.

urlProfile.title: Connection string
urlProfile.description: Style B - a single connection string, as handed out by Neon, Supabase, Railway or RDS.

url.description: postgres:// or postgresql:// connection string. Use ${VAR} and keep the real value in .env - it embeds the password. Special characters in the password must be percent-encoded (@ as %40, / as %2F).

fieldsProfile.title: Discrete fields
fieldsProfile.description: Style A - host, database, user and password as separate fields.

host.description: Hostname or IP of the database server.

user.description: Login role. Use a dedicated READ-ONLY user (see sql/create_readonly_user.sql), never your application or owner user.

password.description: Use ${VAR} and keep the real value in .env. A literal password here is a leak waiting to happen - this file is meant to stay secret-free so it can be mounted into Docker and shared. Empty string is allowed for trust/peer authentication.
